observed_title: The Charnes–Cooper Transformation and Fractional Programs with Convex Polynomials

read_ranges.scope: entire paper including preliminaries, all main results and proofs, example, conclusion and references

topic_relevance.A01: direct: studies fractional programming and the Charnes–Cooper transformation; derives attainment, duality and SOS/SDP hierarchy results for convex polynomial data.

definitions.name: fractional program (FP)
definitions.statement: inf_{x∈K} f(x)/g(x), with g>0 on K (in the main polynomial section K={h_i≤0}, f,−g,h_i convex polynomials, and f≥0 on K).

definitions.name: Charnes–Cooper transformation (CCT)
definitions.statement: s=x/g(x), t=1/g(x); the exact reformulation uses t>0, s/t∈K and t g(s/t)=1, with perspective objective t f(s/t).

definitions.name: relaxed perspective feasible set K_≤
definitions.statement: t>0, s/t∈K, and 1−t g(s/t)≤0; it is a convex relaxation when K is convex and −g is convex. Equal optimal values with the exact transform require f≥0 on K.

definitions.name: SOS-convex polynomial
definitions.statement: A polynomial f is SOS-convex when its Hessian factors as F(x)F(x)^T for a polynomial matrix F. The paper uses the implication SOS-convex ⇒ convex and moment Jensen inequality.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma 3.2 (relaxed CCT equality)
theorem_cards.statement: The exact CCT problem (P0) and the relaxed perspective problem (eP) have the same infimum; every exact-transform optimum is an optimum of the relaxed problem. Their optimizer sets need not be equal.
proof_steps: K_=⊆K_≤ gives inf(P0)≥inf(eP).
Every relaxed point is a radial scaling τ≥1 of an exact-transform point.
The perspective objective scales by τ and is nonnegative, so the relaxed point cannot improve the exact optimum.
The paper supplies a counterexample to equality of optimizer sets when f vanishes.
gaps: Proof uses g>0 to define the scaling; the conclusion is false without f≥0.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.1 (attainment and equivalence)
theorem_cards.statement: The fractional optimum is attained; the convex CCT reformulation also attains its minimum, with t g(s/t)=1 at an optimizer and equal optimal values.
proof_steps: Set r*=inf(FP), and Φ=f−r*g; positivity of g makes Φ≥0 on K.
A ratio-minimizing sequence and the bound g≤M show inf_K Φ=0.
The cited minimizer theorem for convex polynomial optimization gives x* attaining Φ=0.
Map x* to (s*,t*)=(x*/g(x*),1/g(x*)); Lemmas 3.1–3.2 transfer optimality to PCCT.
gaps: The upper bound on g is essential; Example 4.1 shows nonattainment without it.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.2 (strong duality)
assumptions: Slater point for the original constraints h_i(x)≤0
polynomial-section assumptions and positivity conditions for FP
theorem_cards.statement: The CCT primal PCCT and its Lagrange dual LD have equal values, and the dual maximum is attained.
proof_steps: Construct strict feasibility in PCCT from a Slater point by choosing t=(1+ε)/g(x̂), s=tx̂.
Separate the convex primal image set from points below the primal optimum.
Show the multiplier on the objective coordinate is positive; normalize it to obtain feasible dual multipliers.
Take t→0+ in the separating inequality to recover a dual value at least the primal value; weak duality gives equality.
gaps: Requires the finite-dimensional convex separation setup used in the paper; does not justify strong duality outside stated convex/Slater setting.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.3 (asymptotic SOS hierarchy)
assumptions: A2: f≥0 and g>0 on K
theorem_cards.statement: The SOS relaxation values sup(D_r) converge as r→∞ to max(LD)=inf(FP). Each relaxation value is a lower bound on the fractional minimum.
proof_steps: For feasible (λ,γ,η), the SOS polynomial is globally nonnegative; restricting to K and using h_i≤0 gives f/g≥γ−Cη.
Compactness and g>0 give g_min>0; choose L above the radius of K and C>2/g_min.
Apply the cited high-degree perturbation result to a nonnegative dual polynomial on the scaled cube; the SOS perturbation ε_r tends to zero.
Use strong duality from Theorem 4.2 to identify the limiting value.
gaps: No explicit convergence rate or finite level is given for arbitrary convex polynomial data; numerical SDP output alone is not a proof.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.4 (moment dual and rank-one extraction)
assumptions: optimal Q_r moment solution with ȳ_0≠0
theorem_cards.statement: max(D_r)=inf(Q_r); under the stated rank-one and nonzero-mass conditions, x̄=(L_ȳ(x_i)/ȳ_0)_i is an optimal solution of FP.
proof_steps: Build a strictly feasible moment sequence by pushing forward positive measure from a neighborhood of a strictly feasible CCT point; this gives SDP strong duality.
Rank one plus the Hankel moment structure gives ȳ_α=ȳ_0 x̄^α.
The Q_r inequalities imply original feasibility and 1/ȳ_0≥g(x̄).
Compare primal and dual objective values to force equality and optimality.
gaps: Rank-one condition is sufficient, not asserted necessary. The example later reports numerical rank one only approximately and separately verifies its candidate analytically.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.5 (SOS-convex exact first level)
assumptions: optimal Q′ solution ȳ with ȳ_0≠0
theorem_cards.statement: inf(FP)=max(D′)=inf(Q′); the first SOS relaxation is exact, and x̄=(L_ȳ(x_i)/ȳ_0)_i is optimal.
proof_steps: SOS-convexity plus a minimizer of the nonnegative dual polynomial shows that polynomial is SOS, making the Lagrange dual optimizer feasible for D′.
Strict feasibility of Q′ gives SDP strong duality.
Normalize ȳ by ȳ_0, apply the SOS-convex moment Jensen inequality to constraints, −g and f, then sandwich objective values.
gaps: The first-level exactness depends on SOS-convexity, stronger than ordinary convexity.

constant_dependence.explicit: Choose L>max_{x∈K}||x|| and C>2/g_min, where g_min=min_K g>0. Set Θ_r(x)=Σ_j(x_j/L)^{2r}; the penalized dual objective is γ−Cη.
constant_dependence.dependence: The valid penalty constant depends on the positive minimum of denominator g over compact K; scaling L depends on the radius of K. The paper proves perturbation error ε_r→0 but gives no general numerical rate. SDP size grows with the monomial/moment dimension s(n,2r).

endpoint_limits.denominator: g must remain strictly positive on K; points with g=0 are outside the transformation and need separate modeling.
endpoint_limits.relaxation: f≥0 on K is used to equate exact and inequality CCT values.
endpoint_limits.attainment: sup_K g<∞ is required for the stated attainment theorem; bounded K is later imposed for the SOS hierarchy.
endpoint_limits.convexity: Ordinary convex polynomial data support asymptotic convergence; finite first-level exactness requires SOS-convexity.
endpoint_limits.algorithm: No claim that every SDP solver output is an exact certificate; numerical rank evidence in the example is approximate.

reusable_methods.method: Charnes–Cooper homogenization for a single positive-denominator ratio
reusable_methods.transfer: Can normalize a ratio objective into lifted (s,t) variables when the transformed feasible constraints/objective meet the paper’s convexity assumptions. For the maximal-cube operator interface, keep the original cube center, scale, and input shared across every transformed constraint; CCT alone does not establish that coupling.
If replacing equality tg(s/t)=1 by ≥1, explicitly prove numerator nonnegativity; otherwise the radial scaling can lower the objective.

reusable_methods.method: SOS dual lower certificates and moment recovery
reusable_methods.transfer: Use SOS feasibility as a verifiable lower-bound certificate and rank-one moments as a sufficient recovery path; report hierarchy limit separately from finite-level exactness.

unchecked: Paper text was read in full. I independently checked the algebraic CCT inverse, radial scaling argument, weak-duality direction, and the stated dependence on g_min/L. I did not independently prove the cited external lemmas (convex polynomial minimizer, SOS perturbation theorem, SOS-convex Jensen lemma, SDP Slater theorem), reproduce the SOS hierarchy in a solver, or verify the paper’s numerical example. These are author-reported claims conditional on those cited results.
